extracted.intended_audience: journalists and journalism educators covering disability issues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for journalists and newsrooms on how to report about people with disabilities, how to represent disability in media, and how to make journalism itself more accessible and inclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical resources to help journalists better report on disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: “The center’s aim is to provide practical resources to help journalists better report on disabilities and people with disabilities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The center expects reporters to consult it when they have questions (for example, on how to describe a disability or where to find a particular resource), to see what other reporters are doing, and to share practices that advance depth and quality of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain journalistic role; not an advocacy group
rubrics_metrics.description: “This isn’t an advocacy group. It’s a place for journalists to better their craft.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and resources are framed to improve reporting craft and accuracy while preserving journalistic independence rather than promoting advocacy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid caricature; ensure accuracy and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed problem: “people with disabilities were often caricaturized and that news about disabilities was often inaccurate or incomplete.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should avoid stereotyped or caricatured portrayals and strive for reporting that is factually accurate and complete in context and detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate descriptions and language for disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should know “how to describe a disability.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unsure about terminology or descriptions, reporters should consult resources or experts (including the center) to use respectful, accurate, and preferred language and to avoid ableist phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance the depth and quality of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The center encourages work that “advances the depth and quality of coverage in this important area.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for in-depth, contextual, and explanatory reporting rather than superficial or token mentions; share exemplary work and methods among peers to raise standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training, seminars, and curriculum for reporters and newsrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: The center and its leaders have a history of conducting presentations, seminars and developing curricula to educate reporters (e.g., Levine’s presentations; Gilger’s seminars; Wendy Lu’s curriculum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms and reporters are encouraged to undertake or attend training on disability reporting, newsroom management, ethics, and inclusive practices to improve coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote inclusive representation of people with disabilities in media
rubrics_metrics.description: Work to “promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in mass media worldwide” and improve representation across news, entertainment, and online media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include disabled people’s perspectives, avoid erasure or stereotyped roles, and engage with disability communities to reflect diverse lived experiences accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make journalism accessible to audiences with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop “plain language translations and other ways of making journalism more accessible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accessible formats and practices (plain language, audio description, captioning, clear layout, etc.) so journalism is reachable and usable by people with diverse disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and mentor disabled journalists and professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: The center and advisors engage in mentoring, fellowships, and informal support for disabled journalists (e.g., mentoring roles, fellowship programs, judging of awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage mentorship, fellowships, and career support to increase the pipeline and retention of disabled journalists in the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rigorous, data-driven and precision journalism techniques where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors bring expertise in “computer-assisted reporting” and “precision journalism techniques” that can inform coverage of disability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply data, demographics, public-opinion polling, and other empirical methods to deepen reporting, reveal structural issues, and improve accuracy in stories about disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and incentivize excellence in disability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The center and its allies participate in judging and awarding reporting (e.g., Katherine Schneider Journalism Award for Excellence in Disability Reporting) to uphold standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards, fellowships, and judged recognition are used to highlight exemplary work and set models for the field.
